exponential_foreground — VIDEOSTREAM recursive op

• Data kinds: video → video

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.exponential_foreground(video, alpha: 'float' = 0.05, threshold: 'float' = 0.1) -> 'np.ndarray' (to call the implementation directly, import videostream; videostream.exponential_foreground(video, alpha: 'float' = 0.05, threshold: 'float' = 0.1) -> 'np.ndarray'; from the registry, opsvideostream.get("exponential_foreground"))

Usage

Foreground masks |frame − exponential background| > threshold → 0/1 (T, H, W) (video).

Runs the same exponential moving average bg += α (frame - bg) as exponential_background, and in each frame sets to 1 the difference from the updated bg, |frame - bg| > threshold. The first frame is used to initialise bg and its difference is 0, so t = 0 is all pixels 0.

• video: a (T, H, W) array or a list of 2-D frames. Integer dtypes are normalised to [0, 1] by their maximum, float is clipped. NaN/Inf gives ValueError.

• alpha: [0, 1]. The larger it is, the faster the background follows, and a stopped object disappears in about 1/α frames. With 1, bg == frame, so all pixels are always 0.

• threshold: in intensity units of [0, 1]. It is an absolute threshold common to all pixels, so noise in dark regions and noise in bright regions are cut by the same threshold.

• Returns: (T, H, W) float64 of 0 / 1.

• Failure: ValueError.

To set the threshold from per-pixel variance, running_gaussian_foreground. For motion detection without ghosts, three_frame_difference.
